messages.subject: remaining to-do for 1.0.2
parts:
1.0.2 is almost ready.

The remaining to-do item is to get all
of the distributions to return -infinity
when inputs are out of support. This could
wait -- the behavior right now is to throw
std::domain_error, which also results in
samples being rejected.

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] remaining to-do for 1.0.2
parts:
test_grad would be great -- it's really useful
in tracking down misspecified models that fail
due to NaN/infinite values or gradients.

Depending on when Stan 1.0.2's done, we could release
that first. RStan has to wait for the official Stan
version for synch anyway. And RStan release can be done
in addition to Stan releases, though I'm not sure
I want to go down to things like 1.0.2.1 in release
numbers!

We need to get get more of a dump available from
the Stan side for these on the fly to implement
some of Michael B's suggested diagnostics. Then
we'll get new structures because we get positions,
momentums (don't make me say "momenta"), and
gradients per leapfrog step.

- Bob

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] remaining to-do for 1.0.2
parts:
I just pushed the rework of the vectorization stuff I was working on.
I think it can still be improved for readability / maintainability,
but I was able to reduce the number of template specializations and
extended some of the functionality.

In short, it does the same thing, but with less code. I have also been
more careful about the reusuable subexpressions in the vectorized
probability distributions. I don't think we're down to the minimum
number of calls, but we're getting closer.

I'm ready, as long as I didn't introduce any bugs.
